items.summary: Google has paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program until next year, citing a significant rise in automated submissions. The company stated that the vast majority of these reports are invalid or contain hallucinations, overwhelming engineers and maintainers. Google promised an update in the first quarter of 2027 and encouraged participants to explore other bug bounty programs.
items.title: Google Pauses Open Source Bug Bounty Program Due to AI Spam

items.summary: As organizations adopt lakehouse architectures, data is moving from proprietary warehouses to open formats like Parquet. However, true openness requires the ability to move data between catalogs without duplication or data loss. To address this, Unity Catalog introduced the REGISTER and UNREGISTER endpoints to the Apache Iceberg REST catalog specification. These APIs allow users to attach tables to new catalogs and explicitly remove them from old ones, preventing 'split-brain' scenarios where multiple catalogs manage the same data. This ensures seamless portability and a single source of truth for table metadata.
items.title: Unity Catalog Introduces REGISTER and UNREGISTER APIs for Data Portability

items.summary: Daniel Kreiss and Lorcan Neill from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill argue that social media platforms should adopt a 'militant democracy' framework to counter threats to democratic governance. Published in the journal Information, Communication & Society, their paper suggests platforms must prioritize democratic principles over state regulation, particularly in contexts where governments are undergoing democratic backsliding or have become authoritarian. The authors contend that platforms, as integral communicative institutions, have a responsibility to prevent anti-democratic actors from seizing power and to protect opposition voices. Citing the rapid decline of democracy in the United States, Brazil, and other nations, they urge trust and safety executives to make proactive decisions regarding content moderation. The framework calls for platforms to override immediate business interests to safeguard free and fair elections and democratic norms, drawing on historical precedents where platforms successfully de-platformed figures like Donald Trump following January 6th.
items.title: Scholars Propose Militant Democracy Framework for Social Media Platforms

items.summary: Microsoft and Hugging Face introduced ThinkingBox, a benchmark evaluating AI agents on stateful business workflows. The study found that while many agents can perform tasks correctly once, they frequently fail to maintain consistency across repeated trials. Analysis of 121,680 trials across 12 models revealed that 79,853 attempts failed executable checks, with errors often stemming from tool handling rather than reasoning. The benchmark calculates cost per successful task and cost per dependable task to assess efficiency and reliability. Results indicate that high single-attempt accuracy does not guarantee dependability, urging developers to verify terminal database states rather than relying on agent summaries. The open-source environment allows users to reproduce these evaluations.
items.title: ThinkingBox Benchmarks AI Agents on Consistency and Cost

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced a rebranding of artificial intelligence to super intelligence, accompanied by a non-binding safety pact signed by major tech executives. Participants on TechCrunch’s Equity podcast expressed skepticism regarding the pact’s legal weight, noting its voluntary nature and a misspelling of the United States on the document. While Trump described the agreement as morally binding, analysts highlighted the stark contrast between his previous anti-regulation stance and the recent collaboration with CEOs like Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, and Elon Musk. The meeting appears to serve as a rebranding exercise aimed at alleviating fears that super intelligence poses less risk than traditional AI, though underlying tensions between the administration and companies like Anthropic remain unresolved.
items.title: Trump Renames AI to Super Intelligence Amid Safety Pact Skepticism

items.summary: The AI industry is booming, yet women are increasingly left behind, facing a "permanent underclass" with limited upward mobility. While AI roles offer high pay, women comprise only about a quarter of new hires in these positions, compared to 50% in non-AI roles, and just 13% in executive positions. Men earn a median $45,000 more than women in AI occupations. Experts attribute this to hiring networks favoring men, aggressive scaling back of diversity programs, and a culture demanding long hours that disproportionately affects women, particularly after maternity leave. Advocates warn this trend could create the greatest gender pay gap in generations.
items.title: Women Face Growing Exclusion in the Rapidly Expanding AI Industry

items.summary: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts language model designed for English and German. The model features 78.1B total parameters with only 3.46B active per token, enabling efficient deployment on regulated hardware like NVIDIA B200 or H200 GPUs. Developed end-to-end by teams in Germany and Finland, Kolibri targets sovereign deployment in public administration and aerospace. It adheres to the EU AI Act and GDPR, utilizing a 128,000-token vocabulary optimized for German text. Benchmarks show it leads in English agentic tasks and ties with Qwen3.5 on average performance, while supporting up to 1,048,576 tokens of context via a hybrid attention mechanism.
items.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Bilingual German-English MoE Model Kolibri

items.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense signed a contract with Overview Energy to develop a space-based solar power system capable of beaming energy to Earth. The Pentagon aims to deploy a demonstration by 2028, with full satellite constellation deployment starting in 2030. Overview Energy also secured a deal with Meta for up to 1 gigawatt of power. While proponents highlight 24-hour energy generation, critics question the technology's economic viability.
items.title: Pentagon Contracts with Overview Energy for Space Solar Project

items.summary: As utility-scale solar and wind farms face land scarcity and legal pushback, floating power plants are emerging as a critical solution for expanding clean energy capacity. These technologies, which include floating solar, tidal, wave, and nuclear systems, can provide permanent energy for cities like Pevek and Luanda or temporary power for mining and emergencies. Prototypes are being tested globally, from Russia's floating nuclear plants to the University of Michigan's wave energy devices on Beaver Island. Experts suggest offshore floating solar could offer higher efficiency than land-based systems due to seawater cooling, presenting a strategic alternative for nations with limited land resources while enhancing energy security and resilience.
items.title: Floating Power Plants Offer New Energy Solutions Amid Land Constraints

items.summary: An author visited dealers in Sao Paulo to report on the rapid rise of Chinese electric vehicles in Brazil. Leapmotor, BYD, Great Wall Motors, and Geely are establishing local assembly plants to reduce dependence on imports. BYD operates a large facility in Camaçari, while Geely has invested in a Renault do Brasil plant. Sales figures indicate strong market penetration for brands like BYD and Great Wall Motors, with specific models outselling established competitors. The article highlights a strategic shift from importing vehicles to manufacturing them locally within Brazil.
items.title: Chinese EV makers expand Brazil operations with local factories

items.summary: Global plugin vehicle registrations rose 5% year over year in August, reaching approximately 1.8 million units. Pure battery electric vehicles (BEVs) drove this growth with a 13% increase, representing 73% of plugin sales, while plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) declined 12%. Excluding the US and China, EV sales jumped 53% in July. In the global top 20, the Tesla Model Y remained the leader despite a 12% drop, followed by the Geely Xingyuan and BYD Song. Toyota surpassed Volkswagen to become the best-selling legacy brand, aided by the return of the RAV4 PHEV. Market share for the top five OEMs decreased year on year, indicating a diversifying market with rising competition from brands like Leapmotor and Zeekr.
items.title: Global EV Sales Surge Led by BEVs and Chinese Models in August

items.summary: Thieves in California stole two PlusAI trailers marked with Nvidia branding, expecting valuable AI hardware. Police recovered them hours later, finding they contained only sand used for weight simulation during autonomous truck testing. No equipment was damaged.
items.title: PlusAI Trailers Stolen for Nvidia Branding Found Filled with Sand

items.summary: Google launched the Fitbit Air in India for ₹13,999, positioning it as a screenless health tracker. It distinguishes itself from cheaper competitors like Noise REP and Amazfit Helio Strap through a Gemini AI-powered Health Coach, which requires a separate Google Health Premium subscription.
items.title: Google launches Fitbit Air in India at ₹13,999

items.summary: Australia's electric vehicle market saw an unprecedented boost in 2026, with EVs accounting for 25.8% of total sales. Chinese carmaker BYD has emerged as a formidable competitor, selling over 68,000 vehicles in the first eight months of 2026 to become Australia's second-highest-selling brand. Globally, BYD's sales surged from about 190,000 in 2020 to 4.6 million in 2025. The company attributes its success to vertical integration, a diverse product range including plug-in hybrids, and its Blade Battery technology. Despite facing cybersecurity scrutiny and safety concerns, BYD continues to challenge established automotive brands.
items.title: BYD Reshaping Australia's EV Market Amid Global Growth

items.summary: Emma Claassen, founder of the Women in Scaffolding Association, responds to Adrian Chiles regarding a recruitment crisis in Britain's scaffolding industry. She argues that the conversation should focus on attracting capable people regardless of gender rather than traditional demographics. Claassen emphasizes that while the industry needs to widen its pool, standards must remain high and the work cannot be automated. She highlights that some of the next generation will be women.
items.title: Letter argues for recruiting women into scaffolding to address skills shortage

items.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk announced on October 4 that he would rename the company's AI unit to SpaceXSI. He confirmed the change in response to a user inquiry on X, citing US President Donald Trump's advocacy for the term "super intelligence" over "artificial intelligence." At the time of reporting, the account had not yet been updated, and no timeline or further details were provided. SpaceXAI did not immediately respond to comment requests.
items.title: Elon Musk Announces Renaming of SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI

items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that Labour must fulfill its promise to end the leasehold system, criticizing current measures as insufficient. While acknowledging steps like capping fees, the paper highlights soaring service charges and the lack of action on maintenance costs. It questions whether proposed reforms offer a credible exit from dependency or merely regulate subservience, urging ministers to provide a clear path to ownership control.
items.title: Guardian Editorial Urges Labour to Deliver Leasehold Reforms

items.summary: The author wrote a blurb for Ethan Mollick's new book, Coexistence. The text suggests that humans appreciate those who value them and are not overly fearful of them, drawing a parallel to artificial intelligence. The author expresses hope that readers will show appreciation for Mollick's work, stating the book is deserving. Readers are directed to order the book through a provided link.
items.title: Author Encourages Readers to Support Ethan Mollick's New Book on AI

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warned that granting artificial intelligence religious authority or surrendering human judgment to it creates a real safety issue. His comments follow reports that rival company Anthropic consulted religious and philosophical thinkers regarding AI consciousness and morality. Other technology executives, including Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman, have also expressed concern about developing AI systems that appear conscious.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Warns Against Treating AI With Religious Authority

items.summary: About 200 people attended a forum in the Victorian seat of Ripon where candidates debated renewable energy lines, an emergency services levy, and road conditions. Sitting Labor member Martha Haylett and One Nation candidate Donna Buxton were absent. Jo Armstrong opposed the renewable push, while Tim Drylie called for better compensation. The event served as a temperature check ahead of the November 28 election.
items.title: Candidates Debate Renewables and Taxes at Ripon Forum

items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen are attending a pre-COP meeting in Fiji ahead of the main conference. Meanwhile, Assistant Minister Julian Hill highlighted a 55 per cent rise in legal tobacco sales in Queensland following new enforcement laws. Opposition MP Barnaby Joyce proposed building coal-fired power stations, a plan criticized by Labor MP Josh Burns as 'mad'.
items.title: Albanese heads to Fiji for pre-COP climate talks amid domestic political debates

items.summary: Brazil's presidential election polls closed Sunday in a tight contest between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Results are expected within hours. Current polling shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, with a runoff on October 25 likely if neither exceeds 50%. Lula vows to defeat the far right, while Bolsonaro calls for change and pledges to pardon his father if elected.
items.title: Brazil Polls Close in Tight Lula-Bolsonaro Race

items.summary: Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe, an 18-year-old P-plater, was refused bail after his car struck a crowd of Newcastle Knights supporters, injuring nine people. A five-year-old girl remains in an induced coma while others recover. Samarasinghe faces nine charges, including dangerous driving. Chris Clancy described the sudden crash on wet ground. The community has rallied to support victims, with fundraisers established.
items.title: Driver Denied Bail After Newcastle Crash Injured Nine Fans Including Child

items.summary: The Yemen presidency announced a military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, despite the group making fresh gains and effectively encircling the government-held city of Taiz. Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen's presidential council, declared the start of operations to extend state authority across the national territory. Fighting around Taiz has killed more than 70 people, with sources reporting the isolation of the city from Aden. While the government struggles to roll back the Houthi surge even with Saudi support, experts like Farea Al-Muslimi of Chatham House downplayed expectations of the offensive's success, calling it meaningless. Residents of Taiz vowed to resist any Houthi advance.
items.title: Yemen Presidency Announces Military Drive to Retake Houthi Territory Amid Taiz Siege

items.summary: Polls closed in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Sunday evening for the general election, with 3.4 million voters eligible. Preliminary results show early leads for nationalist candidates in the presidency. The election occurs amidst economic challenges and ethnic divisions, with former leader Milorad Dodik barred from office but remaining influential. Results are expected late Sunday.
items.title: Polls Close in Bosnia-Herzegovina's Divisive Election Amidst Ethnic Tensions

items.summary: Wakana Koga won the -48kg gold medal, defeating Assunta Scutto in the final. Ahmad Yusifov secured gold in the -60kg category after coming from behind to beat Sherzod Davlatov. Both victories occurred on the opening day of the 2026 World Championships in Baku, Azerbaijan. Medals were awarded by Azerbaijan's Mr Azer ALIYEV and International Judo Federation's Mr Timur KEMELL.
items.title: Koga and Yusifov Win Gold at 2026 Judo World Championships in Baku

items.summary: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election pits incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls closed at 17:00 BRT. Lula, 80, seeks a third term despite term limits preventing a 2030 run. Flávio, 45, campaigns while his father serves a 27-year sentence. Minas Gerais is viewed as a critical bellwether state for the outcome.
items.title: Brazil 2026 Presidential Race Features Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro

items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is considering calling an early general election after Congress rejected two housing measures. While 29 November is the earliest possible date, no decision has been made. Sánchez is consulting coalition partners and weighing public protests against the government's proposals to extend eviction protections and regulate rentals.
items.title: Spanish PM Weighs Early Election After Housing Bill Rejection

items.summary: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned on October 5, 2026, without stated reasons, according to state media. Hamid Bovard, CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company, is now acting minister. President Dr. Pezeshkian accepted the resignation. Paknejad previously noted that oil revenues would continue. The resignation occurs during a seven-month war between Iran and the U.S., which pressures the economy.
items.title: Iran's Oil Minister Resigns Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: The article discusses the Japanese term 'shinjū,' historically associated with lovers' suicides in literature and theater. It notes that the term also applies to other categories like family and parent-child suicides. The text raises a question regarding whether such deaths can be classified as suicides when the child lacks the capacity to consent, highlighting the complexity of the terminology.
items.title: Japan Updates Terminology for Parent-Child Deaths

items.summary: Three female journalists accused Delhi police officers of sexual harassment during protests in the capital. The Delhi Police acknowledged receiving the complaint and transferred it to the crime branch for a fair inquiry. Videos showed protesters being dragged from the Jantar Mantar site. Activist Aahna Singh stated police dragged her by her hair and resorted to brutality. The Press Club of India demanded immediate action, calling the behavior unacceptable in a democracy.
items.title: Journalists Accuse Indian Police of Harassment During Delhi Protests

items.summary: Yemen's internationally recognised government announced an all-out war to reclaim territory held by the Houthis. President Rashad al-Alimi declared military operations to retake the republic's territory. The announcement follows recent exchanges of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, including attacks on Saudi oil sites. While the government claims to be weakening Houthi capabilities, security sources indicate the group continues to make gains and control key areas like Taiz.
items.title: Yemeni Government Announces War to Reclaim Territory from Houthis

items.summary: Media reports indicate the flydubai co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, likely acted alone in an apparent bid to crash the Israel-bound flight. Israeli officials and sources suggest no link to a group or government exists yet. The UAE leads the investigation, which found the suspect attempted a terrorist act. The flight, carrying 174 passengers, made a rapid descent of over 17,000 feet before landing in Saudi Arabia.
items.title: Flydubai Co-pilot Accused of Lone-Wolf Hijacking Attempt

items.summary: A military court in eastern DR Congo sentenced 27 soldiers to death for cowardice after they withdrew from the front line during fighting against AFC/M23 rebels in Uvira. The trial involved 112 soldiers from the 21st Simba Battalion. While 54 received five-year sentences and 10 got six-month terms, 21 were acquitted due to insufficient evidence. This follows a similar May ruling against 58 soldiers.
items.title: DR Congo Court Sentences 27 Soldiers to Death for Cowardice

items.summary: Japanese police arrested a 20-year-old U.S. Marine on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman in Naha, Okinawa, officials said Sunday. The suspect was found walking alone after security footage showed him entering the hotel with the victim. Okinawa Governor Genta Koja expressed outrage, citing the case as a major shock to residents living near U.S. bases. The U.S. Marine Corps stated it takes the allegations seriously and is cooperating with authorities.
items.title: Japanese police arrest U.S. Marine in alleged murder case on Okinawa

items.summary: Ethiopian federal forces reportedly recaptured Mekelle airport from Tigrayan fighters, according to unnamed city sources speaking to The Associated Press. While a general confirmed military control, neither the Ethiopian government nor the Tigray People's Liberation Front issued official statements. Uncertainty remains regarding the exact timing of the recapture and whether fighting occurred, as severe network disruptions hinder verification.
items.title: Ethiopian Forces Recapture Mekelle Airport Amid Uncertainty

items.summary: Khanh Nguyen Phu, a Vietnamese nationalized resident in Japan, observes a significant shift in attitudes toward foreign nationals since his arrival in 2014. While he initially encountered politeness, he notes that by 2026 the environment has become politically charged. Disinformation has unsettled the community, leading some to question their futures. Nguyen Phu, who speaks English and Japanese, highlights the struggles of unskilled workers compared to his own smooth integration.
items.title: Vietnamese Scholar Notes Rising Anti-Immigrant Tension in Japan

items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced a new aid package worth more than 1.3 billion euros ($1.5 billion) for Ukraine during a visit to Kyiv on Sunday. The agreement includes approximately 1 billion euros for weapons, including combat drones, and 350 billion euros to support Ukraine's energy sector. Merz stated that these barbarous attacks on the civilian population must stop and called for European unity against Russia. Meanwhile, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko urged the capital to be on a war footing due to round-the-clock attacks on residential areas and infrastructure.
items.title: German Chancellor Merz Announces Aid Package for Ukraine Amidst Russian Attacks

items.summary: Bosnia is proceeding with a general election on Sunday, a process dominated by political parties closely linked to the ethnic divisions of the 1990s war. The vote will select numerous officials across multiple government tiers within a complex system established by the 1995 peace deal to maintain the partitioned country. FRANCE 24 correspondent Laurent Rouy reports from Belgrade on the event.
items.title: Bosnia Holds General Election Amid Persistent Ethnic Divisions

items.summary: Carl Cederström, a sociologist at Stockholm Business School, argues in his book 'The Wellness Syndrome' that wellness has transformed from a countercultural trend into a corporate tool designed to increase productivity rather than happiness. He explains that concepts like mindfulness and calorie counting have been corporatized, creating a moral imperative for individuals to optimize their health. Cederström suggests this focus on individual improvement fosters 'passive nihilism,' where people retreat into personal routines to avoid engaging with broader societal or political issues. He notes that while wellness activities offer a sense of order, they do not guarantee genuine well-being or happiness.
items.title: Sociologist Carl Cederström critiques wellness as a corporate productivity tool

items.summary: As the Russian invasion of Ukraine approaches its fifth year, the Kremlin employs complex networks to circumvent Western sanctions. A7, a financial structure founded in Kyrgyzstan and led by Ilan Shor, utilizes shell companies in jurisdictions like Hong Kong and Turkey to obscure Russian funds. The network processes payments via a stablecoin, A7A5, and falsifies invoices to disguise military equipment purchases. Investigations suggest the system moved over $6.9 billion through international banks. Additionally, European banks like Raiffeisen Bank remain key channels for gas exports, with fees reaching 15% on transfers. The Kremlin also leverages cryptocurrencies, with Shor reporting between 1,500 and 2,000 daily transactions in 2024.
items.title: Kremlin Uses Shell Companies and Crypto to Evade Sanctions

items.summary: Ex-RBI Governor Das stated India's real GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter of the current financial year. He noted growth just exceeds 8% for the period July-September 25-26 to April-June 26-27. Das emphasized structural reforms and productive capabilities for resilient long-term expansion while highlighting digital governance savings of around Rs 5.1 lakh crore.
items.title: Ex-RBI Governor Das Forecasts India Near 8% Growth

items.summary: Indian consumers increasingly prefer subscription models for premium smartphones, viewing devices as products to upgrade rather than own long-term. Experts note that while the market is in an early stage, financing options and assured buyback schemes are driving growth, particularly in the ultra-premium segment. However, overall festive sales are expected to decline due to higher device prices.
items.title: India's Premium Smartphone Market Shifts to Subscription Models

items.summary: Supreme Court Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticized the Special Intensive Revision process for deleting names from voter lists, stating it strikes at the heart of the Constitution. Speaking at Nalsar, Hyderabad, he argued that disenfranchising citizens is arbitrary and that the right to vote is integral to India's freedom. Bhuyan emphasized that no authority can alter Article 326 without notice and hearing.
items.title: Supreme Court Judge Criticizes Voter List Deletion Process

items.summary: The Kerala High Court directed the CBI to investigate the 2012 disappearance of Subash Chandra Bose, a Tripura State Rifles soldier. While the CBI questioned jurisdiction and the likelihood of tracing him after 14 years, the court ordered the inquiry under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, emphasizing that a premier agency should not take a pessimistic view in such cases.
items.title: Kerala High Court Orders CBI Probe into Soldier's 14-Year-Old Disappearance

items.summary: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan announced that the Muziris Heritage Project will become an international heritage tourism destination. He launched water taxis and kayaks during the event, stating plans to expand services to regions like Ezhikkara and Kodungalloor. Tourism Minister P.C. Vishnunadh described the initiative as a potential global tourism model. The government also aims to revive suspended boating services and develop new museums and hotels to boost local businesses and employment.
items.title: Kerala Chief Minister Announces Muziris as International Heritage Tourism Destination

items.summary: A 36-year-old Pakistani undertrial prisoner named Shahid Imran allegedly died by suicide at a high-security central jail in Jammu on Sunday. Officials reported that he was found unconscious in his cell around 5.15 am and was subsequently declared brought dead at GMCH. Imran, a resident of Sargooda district in Pakistan's Punjab, was identified as the deceased.
items.title: Pakistani Undertrial Prisoner Dies by Suicide in Jammu Jail

items.summary: The GST Council in New Delhi is set to unveil GST 2.0 reforms aimed at simplifying business processes and reducing litigation. Proposals include a system of deemed acknowledgement for refunds and registration applications within 10 days, and a target to clear 60% of registration applications in three days. Significant changes address decriminalisation, raising the prosecution threshold to Rs 5 crore and reducing maximum sentences. The reforms also introduce guardrails for e-way bills to prevent harassment of truck drivers and simplify service definitions for exporters. Officials expect these measures to benefit SMEs and improve cash flow for long-gestation projects.
items.title: GST Council Unveils GST 2.0 Reforms for Faster Registration and Easier Refunds

items.summary: A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Missouri, US, after a truck allegedly struck her car. Her family in Mahabubabad has appealed to the government for assistance to transport her remains home for last rites. Another passenger sustained serious injuries and was hospitalized. Details regarding the crash and the injured woman's condition are still awaited.
items.title: Telangana Woman Dies in US Crash; Family Seeks Help

items.summary: Over 700 families living in JJ cluster bastis near the Prime Minister's residence face eviction and relocation to Savda Ghevra. Residents fear losing livelihoods and education after officials threatened demolition. The Centre claims the land is for defence infrastructure, while residents argue relocation must be within a five-kilometre radius. Courts have dismissed their case, and families are now being asked to vacate by October 6, 2026.
items.title: Over 700 families face eviction near PM residence

items.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party intensified protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 5, 2026, demanding his removal and action against a police officer accused of sexual harassment. BJP leaders accused AAP of attempting to vitiate Delhi's political atmosphere. AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj highlighted perceived double standards in police action, while Arvind Kejriwal condemned the detention of his members. At least 25 AAP members were detained during the march.
items.title: AAP Intensifies Protest Against CEC Amid BJP Accusations of Disrupting Order

items.summary: Investigators are searching for suspect Varun Kumar in Delhi after matching his image to footage. Police intensified financial probes into retired IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal's accounts and two disputes worth Rs 1 crore and Rs 4 crore. No direct link to the murder has been established yet. A Rs 50,000 reward was declared for his arrest.
items.title: Police Expand Murder Probe to Delhi Amid Financial Dispute Scrutiny

items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh Agriculture Department has prepared a contingency plan for the Rabi 2026-27 season following uneven rainfall caused by El Nino. The plan divides the state into 10 agro-climatic zones to recommend specific crop varieties based on water availability. It aims to mitigate potential farmer losses by suggesting suitable crops for irrigated, non-irrigated, and semi-irrigated areas across different zones.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh Agriculture Department Prepares Rabi 2026-27 Contingency Plan

items.summary: Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from San Jose, designed an atmospheric water generator to address global water scarcity. By testing low-frequency sine waves, he found they increased water collection by 117 percent compared to silent conditions. His prototype used the Peltier effect to cool air and condense moisture. Burki's project earned him a place among 30 national finalists in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. While the results are promising, further research is needed before the technique can be applied outside controlled prototypes.
items.title: Seventh-grader Ankith Burki boosts water generation with sound

items.summary: Congress general secretary KC Venugopal summoned former Uttarakhand CM Harish Rawat to Delhi amid party concerns over his recent solo political yatras. Leadership fears these independent activities undermine coordinated preparations for the state Assembly elections. Kumari Selja previously wrote to Rawat requesting he stop the programme, citing it as too individualistic. The meeting aims to restore party unity and align Rawat's moves with the Congress poll strategy.
items.title: Congress summons former Uttarakhand CM Harish Rawat over solo yatra concerns

items.summary: The New Employees Health Scheme in Hyderabad has covered 919 hospitals and approved cashless treatment for 15,395 cases since launching on July 17. Total approved treatments are valued at ₹104.63 crore. The scheme includes outpatient services, wellness centres, and emergency admissions for government employees and pensioners, with funds contributed by both employees and the government.
items.title: Telangana NEHS Scheme Covers 919 Hospitals with 15,395 Approved Treatments

items.summary: Telangana targets increasing its renewable-energy capacity from 10,642 MW in 2025-26 to 29,645 MW by 2029-30. The state seeks benefits from the Union Cabinet-approved Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme, pending approval of its transmission and storage projects. Approved plans include 7,800 MW of new capacity, comprising solar, wind, and battery storage, to support grid stability and industrial demand.
items.title: Telangana Aims to Triple Renewable Capacity by 2030 via Central Funds

items.summary: Nishant Kerketta, a fashion and fitness enthusiast from Jharkhand, has gained significant attention on Instagram for his unique content style. His videos juxtapose scenes of him working in rural agricultural settings with carefully styled fashion reveals. One reel challenges the stereotype that men from villages cannot dress well, transitioning from farm work to a polished look featuring a white shirt, denim, and accessories. Viewers have reacted positively, comparing him to fictional characters and praising his style. Kerketta does not separate rural life from fashion, instead using the contrast between his modest village surroundings and his polished outfits as a central theme in his content.
items.title: Jharkhand Fashion Enthusiast Nishant Kerketta Goes Viral for Blending Rural Life with Style

items.summary: A security camp in Abujhmad, Chhattisgarh, has been converted into a hostel for Scheduled Tribe students following improved security conditions. Narayanpur Collector Namrata Jain initiated the project to provide safe accommodation and educational support. The facility serves students from remote villages, addressing logistical challenges and reducing financial burdens on families. It reflects shifting development priorities in the region.
items.title: Security Camp in Abujhmad Converted to Tribal Hostel

items.summary: The Bihar state government suspended seven engineers and initiated proceedings against an official for alleged negligence during the recent floods. While the Gandak River water levels have receded significantly, authorities reported that 9.87 lakh people across six districts remain affected. Relief measures include the distribution of ration packets and the deployment of rescue teams.
items.title: Bihar suspends seven engineers over flood response negligence

items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has outlined various forms for its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls starting in June 2025. Form 6 is for new registrations or restoring deleted names, while Form 7 challenges inclusions or requests deletions. Form 8 handles address changes and other updates, though some voters report confusion regarding its use during SIR. Forms 6A and 6B serve overseas electors and Aadhaar authentication, respectively. Additional forms, such as 9 through 11B, are internal lists maintained by electoral officers to track claims and objections. Kanishka Singharia of Mint reports on these procedures.
items.title: Election Commission Explains Voter Forms for 2025 Electoral Roll Revision

items.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan of the Supreme Court stated that any process disenfranchising millions violates the constitutional order and Articles 14 and 326. Speaking at NALSAR University, he asserted no authority can remove voting rights, calling such acts arbitrary and a negation of the Constitution. This follows the Court's earlier upholding of the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
items.title: SC Judge Condemns Processes That Strip Voting Rights

items.summary: Saint-Gobain plans to invest ₹11,000 crore in India over the next five years, aiming to shift from selling products to offering energy-efficient building solutions. Sreedhar N, the company's Asia-Pacific and India CEO, intends to acquire meaningful assets to expand into construction chemicals and insulation. This investment represents a sharp acceleration compared to the previous decade's spending.
items.title: Saint-Gobain Plans Major India Investment Push

items.summary: A businessline poll indicates most bank economists anticipate the Monetary Policy Committee raising the repo rate by 25 basis points on October 7, 2026. While a majority foresee a cumulative 50-75 bps hike by FY27 to combat inflation, Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis predicts rates will remain unchanged in October, suggesting a potential shift in December. Reasons cited include rising inflation and global central bank actions.
items.title: Bankers Expect MPC Rate Hike Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: Associate Professor Trevor Mazzucchelli of Curtin University explains that while some people appear naturally tidy due to personality traits like conscientiousness, behavior is not fixed. He argues that small, repeated actions create habits and that changing one's environment can prompt new behaviors. Rather than relying solely on motivation, individuals should arrange their surroundings to make desired actions easier, such as placing a key bowl by the door. Consistently performing these new behaviors can eventually alter personality traits. However, Mazzucchelli notes that severe clutter may indicate hoarding disorder, a condition requiring professional help, whereas ordinary messiness can be managed through environmental adjustments and routine changes.
items.title: Psychologist Explains How Habits and Environment Shape Tidiness

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that India has moved beyond mere advocacy to actively engage Moscow and Kyiv in resolving the Ukraine conflict. Speaking at a Munich Leaders' Meeting in New Delhi, he highlighted efforts to ensure Black Sea shipping safety and facilitate grain and energy exports. Jaishankar noted that while India and Russia have historically strong relations dating back to the 1950s, the current geopolitical landscape is marked by a radical repositioning of the United States and the rise of China. He argued that emerging powers are now focusing on diversifying their economies and supply chains through a new architecture of cooperation based on reasonable convergence rather than strict ideological alignment.
items.title: Jaishankar Outlines India's Ukraine Mediation and Global Strategy

items.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan stated that stripping millions of Indians of voting rights is intrinsically arbitrary and violates constitutional guarantees. Speaking at NALSAR University of Law, he argued that the Constitution does not permit two classes of citizens. He warned that such processes undermine the constitutional order and strike at its very heart.
items.title: Justice Bhuyan Calls Disenfranchisement Arbitrary and Unconstitutional

items.summary: Three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by Delhi Police officers while covering protests at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi Police acknowledged the complaints and transferred them to the Crime Branch for an impartial inquiry. The Cockroach Janta Party organized a protest demanding action against the accused officer. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in registering an FIR, while the Press Club of India condemned the police behavior and called for immediate action to protect media freedom.
items.title: Journalists Allegate Sexual Harassment by Delhi Police Officers During Jantar Mantar Protests

items.summary: Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel alleges Rahul Gandhi was too scared to contest from Amethi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, choosing Raebareli instead. Patel claims Akhilesh Yadav persuaded Gandhi to run, warning he would field his own candidate otherwise. Patel also credits the SP-Congress alliance for Congress winning six seats in Uttar Pradesh, where SP secured 37 of the 80 seats.
items.title: SP MP Alleges Rahul Gandhi Feared Contesting Amethi

items.summary: Thousands protested in Delhi on October 4 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged police harassment. The demonstrations, led by student and youth groups, turned violent as protesters breached barricades and clashed with Delhi Police, resulting in hundreds of detentions. Police deployed 5,000 personnel, including riot gear and water cannons, to control the crowds. Separately, supporters protested outside a police station demanding an FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat for allegedly sexually assaulting a journalist. CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat criticized the police response, stating they demanded video evidence of the assault despite the complainant's presence.
items.title: Anti-Gyanesh Kumar Protests Turn Violent in Delhi

items.summary: The Indian government raised the ceiling price for natural gas from difficult fields like the KG-D6 block to $9.89 per MMBtu effective October 1, 2026. This applies to deepwater and ultra-deepwater discoveries through March 31, 2027, according to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell. The ceiling for legacy fields of state-run companies remains at $7 per MMBtu.
items.title: India raises deepwater gas price ceiling to $9.89/MMBtu

items.summary: LKP Securities analyst Rupak De warns investors to remain cautious as the Nifty index breaches its 200-week moving average and slips below the 22,600 support level for the first time since the 2020 crash. De notes this marks the eighth consecutive weekly decline, the longest in 25 years. He advises reducing long exposure until the index decisively moves above 22,600, warning that further drops toward 20,500 are possible if the level holds. De cites historical data showing significant falls in 2008 and 2020 but notes quick reversals in 2011, 2013, and 2016, suggesting outcomes remain uncertain.
items.title: Analyst Warns of Nifty Decline After Breaching Key Support Levels

items.summary: According to profitability scan data from StockEdge.com, seven NSE midcap companies recorded rising earnings per share for four consecutive quarters through June 2026. The list includes Poonawalla Fincorp, FSN E-commerce Ventures, Laurus Labs, Lodha Developers, National Aluminium Company, Bank of India, and Radico Khaitan, each reporting higher EPS than the previous quarter.
items.title: 7 midcap stocks with rising EPS for four straight quarters. Are they in your portfolio?
